recognize_zh: Perls 鐵染色低倍下，骨髓顆粒（particle）以脂肪空泡為主、造血細胞稀少，顆粒內充滿大片深藍色含鐵血黃素沉積，屬 4–5+ 的明顯增加鐵儲存，符合再生不良性貧血等紅血球生成低下時鐵未被利用的表現。
features: Marrow particles composed largely of fat vacuoles with scant hematopoietic cellularity
Heavy, confluent blue (Prussian blue-positive) hemosiderin deposits throughout the particles
Iron stores grade approximately 4-5+ on low-power assessment
Iron located within particle stroma/macrophages rather than dispersed in the smear background
describe_en: Perls (Prussian blue) stain of a bone marrow aspirate at low power shows fatty marrow particles with sparse hematopoietic cells and abundant, confluent blue-staining hemosiderin deposits within the particles. Storage iron is markedly increased (grade approximately 4-5+). Sideroblastic iron in erythroid precursors cannot be assessed at this magnification. In a patient with pancytopenia, the fatty hypocellular particles and increased storage iron are consistent with the findings of aplastic anemia; the diagnosis requires trephine biopsy cellularity assessment.

ddx.vs: Also shows increased storage iron, but particles are normocellular and sideroblasts are reduced, without fatty hypocellular marrow.
Iron is markedly increased with any cellularity, so the history of transfusion and serum ferritin/HFE studies are needed to separate them.
Storage iron is increased but particles are usually cellular and high-power examination shows ring sideroblasts in 15% or more of erythroid precursors.
Morphology of the iron stain cannot distinguish it; dysplasia, blasts and cytogenetic abnormalities on marrow examination favor hypoplastic MDS.
